clue.text: Ruth pinching General Secretary's pen

indicators.note: to pinch is to squeeze or nip, so one word grips the other inside it

parts.note: ruth is an old word for compassion, i.e. pity

explanation.surface: Someone called Ruth steals a fountain pen belonging to a union's general secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruth' looks like a woman's name, but it is the archaic noun for compassion.
explanation.definitionFit: A sty for pigs is a pen, an enclosure for livestock.

clue.text: Student from St Petersburg once with piece of wood for his ruler?

indicators.note: one piece stands in place of another

parts.note: the city was called Leningrad from 1924 to 1991
Lenin, the Soviet ruler, gave the city its name
a post is an upright piece of timber

explanation.surface: A Russian student swapping a wooden stick for a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick of wood, but it is Lenin, the ruler the city was named for.
explanation.definitionFit: A postgraduate is a student continuing study after a first degree.

clue.text: Mature audience's response to pun -cheered

indicators.note: what an audience hears is the spoken word

parts.note: a groan is the usual reply to a pun
to be cheered is to be bucked up

explanation.surface: Listeners respond to a pun by cheering, showing their maturity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audience' sounds like theatre but signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is an adult, someone mature.

clue.text: Reprimanded, as correct answers are not working

parts.note: correct answers are marked with a tick
a machine switched off is not working

explanation.surface: A teacher scolding a pupil as correct answers fail to work.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ticked off is an informal way of saying told off, rebuked.

clue.text: Scaled-down version of blast bomb that may be underfoot on beach?

definitions.text: that may be underfoot on beach?

parts.note: Flip! is a very mild exclamation of annoyance, a toned-down substitute for Blast!
to bomb is to fail badly, as a show that flops

explanation.surface: Sounds like a military briefing about a smaller explosive device left on a beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blast' and 'bomb' paint explosives, but blast is the expletive and bomb is a failure. The definition is cryptic: a sandal worn on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber thong sandal is the typical footwear worn on sand at the seaside.

clue.text: If not digging, stick pike out till rim gets damaged

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: if not digging, plant a stick until the rim breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digging' is slang for liking, and to stick is to put up with, so the definition paraphrases the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom tells someone to accept a situation whether they enjoy it or not.

clue.text: Muriel, removing top, put on a coat

indicators.note: removing the top takes off the first letter

parts.note: Muriel Spark was a Scottish novelist

explanation.surface: Muriel takes off her top and puts on a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muriel' is the novelist Muriel Spark; SPARK loses its top S.
explanation.definitionFit: A parka is a hooded windproof jacket.

clue.text: A word Liberals devised for noble bigwig

indicators.note: devised means made up, so the letters are formed afresh

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for Liberal, and two give LL

explanation.surface: Liberal politicians coin a term for a pompous aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: Law Lords were senior judges sitting in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A Law Lord was a peer holding high judicial office, a titled grandee.

clue.text: Staff boarding front of plane always assembled for take-off

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
boarding means getting on or into, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: ay is an old poetic word for always
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Airline crew boarding the front of a plane, ready for takeoff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take-off' suggests flight but means an imitation; 'assembled' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a mocking imitation, a send-up.

clue.text: Refuse on top of sink spells work!

parts.note: to decline is to refuse
on top of means in addition to, plus
to sink is to drop or fall

explanation.surface: Rubbish piled on the kitchen sink means more chores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like rubbish and 'sink' like the kitchen fitting; both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh's novel and Gibbon's history both bear this title, so it names a literary work.

clue.text: Security measure after spy threat on board

indicators.note: the threat word follows the spy word, so its letters come second in the answer

parts.note: to spot is to see or spy something
on a chessboard, check is the threat to the king

explanation.surface: A security alert issued after a spy threatens people aboard a ship or plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a vessel, but here the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A random inspection is a common precaution used to catch breaches of security.

clue.text: Racket needed by Queen's sports competitor

parts.note: a racket is a noisy din, a row
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A tennis player needs a racket supplied by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' and 'sports' point to tennis, but the racket is a noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who races in boats at a regatta takes part in a sport.

clue.text: Book space for driver: one being instructed to be polite

parts.note: Gen is the short form of Genesis, a book of the Bible
a golfer tees off with a driver from the tee
L, for learner, marks a driver under instruction

explanation.surface: Booking a parking space for a learner driver, who should be courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests cars and L-plates, but the space for a driver is the golf tee.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel describes refined, well-mannered behaviour, a near synonym of courteous.

clue.text: To summarize Origin of Species leaves Darwin so excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up into a new arrangement
the letter leaves, so it is taken away from the other words
the origin of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A nod to Darwin's famous book, imagining its summary thrilled him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes S (first of 'Species') out of DARWINSO, leaving DARWINO; 'excited' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a brief summing-up, meaning briefly or in short.

clue.text: Chap producing contracts for acceptance, briefly

indicators.note: contracts here means holds within, so the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: A man drawing up contracts for someone to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contracts' reads as a noun, but it is a verb meaning contains.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods on appro are supplied on approval, shortened, to be returned if not accepted.

clue.text: Twelve cipher books I'd found in one, with amendments

indicators.note: these pieces are found inside the other word
amendments change the word one into a new order

parts.note: a cipher is a zero, the letter O
NT is the New Testament, a set of books
taken as written

explanation.surface: Twelve books of codes found in one volume, with corrections made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with amendments' rearranges ONE into NOE; 'found in' places the other pieces after its first two letters. Twelve here is the hour, not a count of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Noontide is midday, twelve o'clock.

clue.text: International ordeal something a striker must handle

parts.note: a test is a trial or ordeal
a match is struck to light it

explanation.surface: An international football ordeal that a striker must cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International' and 'striker' paint football, but the striker lights a match. A Test match is an international cricket game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is a cricket game between national sides, so an international fixture.

clue.text: Left wingers in Filipino reviews attack exploitation

indicators.note: the wingers of each word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: Left-wing reviewers in the Philippines attack exploitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left wingers' looks like a political phrase, but 'Left' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsaken means abandoned, left behind.

clue.text: Fungus gives boost to slug

parts.note: to puff something is to promote or boost it
a slug is a bullet, and a ball is shot fired from a gun

explanation.surface: A garden scene: a fungus that encourages slugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slug' looks like the garden pest but is the bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A puffball is a round fungus that bursts to release spores.

clue.text: Ignorant girl with time to reflect

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

indicators.note: reflected in a mirror, the word is reversed

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A girl taking time to reflect on her ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaware means not knowing, ignorant of something.

clue.text: Psychopath regularly cut folk's chins after flipping

indicators.note: flipping turns the picked letters back to front
cutting at regular intervals keeps every other letter

explanation.surface: A deranged person who habitually slashes people's chins.
explanation.walkthrough: Every second letter of FOLKSCHINS gives OKCIS, which 'after flipping' reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicko is slang for a mentally disturbed or perverted person.

clue.text: One taking bow having put together church roof of lead and slate

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: in a down clue the roof is the first letter

parts.note: a slate is a list of candidates for office

explanation.surface: A builder bows after roofing a church with lead and slate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests bowing to applause; it is the bow of a cello. 'Roof', 'lead' and 'slate' all play on building.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellist plays with a bow, so takes up a bow.

clue.text: Peer has nobody to protect name

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a squit is an insignificant person, a nobody

explanation.surface: A lord with no one to guard his title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peer' looks like a noble but is the verb to look.
explanation.definitionFit: To squint is to peer with eyes half closed.

clue.text: Drank as female was eating

parts.note: qua is Latin for in the capacity of, as
fed means ate, took food

explanation.surface: Drinking as a woman did while she was eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Quaffed means drank heartily, in deep draughts.

clue.text: First storey's occupied by just one old girl

indicators.note: occupied by just one means only one of the doubled letter remains inside

parts.note: Floor A is the first level in some lettered buildings

explanation.surface: A ground floor inhabited by one elderly lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old girl' reads as one phrase, but 'old' gives O: FLOOR A keeps only one O.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Flora is a traditional female first name, borne by the Roman goddess of flowers.

clue.text: Comes out with poorly doctor wearing slippers

indicators.note: one piece wears the other, so the doctor goes inside the slippers

parts.note: mules are backless slippers
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor in slippers comes out with something while feeling unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poorly' suggests illness but describes how the words are said.
explanation.definitionFit: To mumble is to say something indistinctly, to utter it badly.

clue.text: State fooled about with satellite coverage

indicators.note: the satellite provides cover, wrapping round the other piece

parts.note: Io is a moon of Jupiter

indicators.note: about turns the word round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to be had is to be fooled

explanation.surface: A government fooled about its satellite broadcasting coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the synonym for fooled; 'coverage' wraps the moon of Jupiter round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Henry, out of practice, comes in second: unfair!

indicators.note: the letter goes out of the first word
the same letter then comes into the second word

parts.note: a habit is a regular practice
a tick is a moment, a second
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man named Henry, rusty from lack of practice, finishes second and protests.
explanation.walkthrough: H leaves HABIT to make ABIT ('out of') and goes into TICK to make THICK ('comes in').
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is a bit thick means it is unreasonable or unjust.

clue.text: Part of body in sound condition becomes afflicted

definitions.note: the definition is singular though the answer is plural: these are parts of the foot

indicators.note: in sound means the words are pronounced, giving the same run of syllables

parts.note: muscle tone is physical condition; ails means is unwell, is afflicted

explanation.surface: A body part in good shape that later falls ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound condition' looks like healthy, but 'in sound' signals that TONE AILS is said aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The horny plates at the tips of the toes are parts of the human body.

clue.text: A little light pressure inflamed leg

parts.note: P is the symbol for pressure
inflamed skin feels hot
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A gentle pressure applied to an inflamed leg.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: A photon is a quantum of light, the smallest particle of it.
